text:
deploy-bot: starting blue/green swap: region routing change: blue -> primary, canary in us-east -> 10%

incident-bot: paging alice (oncall) - elevated error rate (5xx) in us-east canary, threshold exceeded 3m ago :rotating_light:

alice (oncall): on it. pulling up dashboards now. any rollback automated?

dave (prod-sre): seeing 5xx spike from us-east edge -> origin 502s. latency up ~120ms p95 across canary. Logs show connection resets to green pool endpoints.

eva (support): we have two customer reports about timeouts from EU customers, ticket #12345 and #12346. both mention slow responses starting ~10m ago.

carol (eng): I just checked the rollout plan - we switched region weights but DNS TTL was still high for some edge caches (ttl ~300s). possible some clients still hitting green while routing control plane thinks blue.

alice (oncall): timeline: deploy started 2876543200. canary weight 10% us-east. alerts fired 2876543302.

frank (netops): confirming: internal DNS snapshots show mixed A records across edge nodes for us-east, some resolving old-green LB ip. BGP and anycast ok. Looks like stale resolver caches.

alice (oncall): impact classification: partial regional impact, customer-facing timeouts in EU/US-east. severity: high. we should consider immediate mitigation.

dave (prod-sre): suggestion A: flip feature flag kill-switch to route canary to fallback (stable green) until TTLs settle. Suggestion B: abort blueflip and roll back control plane to pre-deploy weights. Which is faster?

carol (eng): fastest is feature-flag flip. rollback involves coordinator + inventory and takes ~5-10m to compute safe weights. flag flip is instant.

alice (oncall): agreed. carol, can you run the flag toggle? provide command.

carol (eng): running toggle now. command: ```
# feature-flagger CLI
ffctl set routing.us-east.canary.enabled false --reason "stale-dns causing split-brain" --by carol
```

carol (eng): executed at 2876543345. Response: 200 OK. New config pushed.

incident-bot: action recorded: routing.us-east.canary.enabled = false by carol at 2876543345.

bob (pager): monitoring: traffic shifted back to green within 30s on control plane. but client-side DNS caches may take up to TTL to refresh. we still see 502s tail.

alice (oncall): let's enable a quick kill-switch layer at the edge to reject new connections if they resolve to stale-green IPs? frank, can you push an ACL to block old-green IPs from being served in us-east for 2m while caches flush?

frank (netops): I can insert an edge deny for the specific IP range. pushing now: ```
# edgectl
edgectl acl add deny ip 10.240.32.0/24 --region us-east --temp 2m --note "block stale-green-ip range"
```

frank (netops): ACL applied at 2876543380 across 3 edge layers.

dave (prod-sre): metrics: error rate falling but still 20% above baseline. p95 latency dropping. Customer tickets: no new ones in last 8m.

eva (support): emailed affected customers with status update, ETA to resolution set to 15 minutes.

alice (oncall): good. escalation: if errors don't normalize by 2876543480 (10m), we'll trigger full rollback. Assign bob to watch metrics, carol to stand by for rollback steps.

bob (pager): watching. setting alert mute for noisy thresholds and keeping a high fidelity trace capture on us-east.

carol (eng): prepping rollback playbook. steps: 1) pause deploy pipeline, 2) set regional weights to previous snapshot, 3) verify healthchecks, 4) unpause. If needed, manual rollback via: ```
# deployctl
deployctl rollback --deploy-id 2026-04-15-1423 --scope region:us-east
```

alice (oncall): note for post-incident: check why control plane didn't detect mixed DNS set earlier and add pre-check for resolver TTLs in rollout gating.

bob (pager): errors back to baseline at 2876543465. p95 latency within 5% of baseline. no additional customer reports.

alice (oncall): great - continuing monitoring for 30m. leaving incident open. handoff: bob -> dave in 25m if stable. carol, please create a short writeup in #postmortems with timestamps and actions.

carol (eng): will do. rough notes to paste into PM: "blueflip partial mismatch due to stale DNS caches; mitigated by feature-flag kill-switch and temporary edge ACL; no full rollback required; customers notified."

dave (prod-sre): filing incident record now and scheduling postmortem 48h window. assign owners: root-cause (carol), mitigation timeline (alice), customer comms (eva), follow-up infra changes (frank).

incident-bot: incident remains open. reminder set for 2876545100 to check stability and close.

alice (oncall): thanks team. quick note: please preserve traces and a sample of failing requests (anonymized) for the postmortem. :thumbsup:

frank (netops): will also capture DNS resolver snapshots and edge cache states.

bob (pager): handoff to dave at 2876543600. I'm leaving the channel to sleep. :wave:

dave (prod-sre): taking over monitoring. will update when incident is closed.

incident-bot: thread archived for follow-ups at 2876545100.
